newsitem.title: SPAIN: Israel to offer final plan for territories in year.
newsitem.headline: Israel to offer final plan for territories in year.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday he would present a proposal for a final settlement with Palestinians on the West Bank and Gaza Strip within one year.

Netanyahu, during a visit to Spain, said Israel would not cede control over the hills surrounding its cities in a final deal. "In the coming year, we will present our version of the final settlement," he told Spanish reporters at a breakfast in Madrid on Wednesday.
The Israeli-Palestinian peace accord stipulated the two sides would agree a permanent arrangement for the disputed territories by May 4, 1999.
At a news conference on Tuesday, Netanyahu said he would not give Palestinians control over airspace or water sources in the territories and would not agree to a Palestinian army.

The Israeli leader, in Madrid to mark five years since the historic Middle East peace conference here in 1991, said he had also come to try to dispel the image of his government in Europe as hardline and opposed to peace.
He has played down problems in the peace process during his visit.

An agreement with Palestinians on a partial Israeli troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron is nearly complete, according to Netanyahu who said Palestinians, not Israelis were stalling a final accord.
"We have pretty much resolved the issue of hot pursuit," he said, referring to a major sticking point of the accord.
Netanyahu said he wished he could expand Jewish settlement in occupied Arab lands faster but fiscal constraints were preventing him.
The prime minister chided Israel's oldest peace partner Egypt for not consistently playing a constructive role in Middle East negotiations.

He said this attitude was problematic because Israel viewed its 17-year peace with Egypt as the cornerstone of a wider Middle East settlement. "In recent years, Egypt has not always played a positive role," Netanyahu said.
His right-wing Israeli government had come under a "consistent cascade of attacks" from Cairo, he said.
Netanyahu said he appealed to Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa to set aside polemics in a meeting on Tuesday on the fringes of a European security summit in Lisbon.
He was vague on the possibility of a territorial compromise with Syria over the disputed Golan Heights. "I have not ruled out a territorial discussion," he said.

Netanyahu came to Spain from a European security summit in Lisbon where he said European leaders, trying to play a greater role in Middle East peacemaking, had not hidden "their questions or criticisms" of Israel.
